Services / Fit-outs & make-good

Fit-outs & make-good.

Commercial alterations, refreshes and end-of-lease work with retained and removed items clearly defined.

Mark the retained and reinstated work clearly.

We turn the proposed work into an itemised scope before organising a commercial fit-out or make-good project. We review the existing condition, tenancy requirements and available plans or photographs. Repairing a local finish, changing a workspace and reinstating a tenancy are handled as distinct briefs.

01 / Office area before tenancy handback

Separate what stays from what goes

Put the agreed handback list next to a room plan. Mark fixtures to retain, remove or make good and where a patch has to meet an adjoining finish. Sequence access, removal, repairs, finishing and cleaning so changed scope can be approved before it is covered by the next trade.

We compare the signed scope, the items that remain and the areas where services or fixings will be exposed after removal. Recording this before stripping out makes it easier to agree patching limits, retained finishes and the condition expected at handover.

For weathered outdoor joinery, we check the timber surface, ends and fixing points before allowing for refinishing or replacement. At an external opening, we review the substrate, old sealant and the existing joint detail before specifying a compatible repair. We price local repairs separately from phased renewal and allow for protection, removal, suitable weather and the product’s return-to-use conditions.

  • Partitions, walls and ceilings

    We identify the included areas, removal limits and repairs to retained construction. Services within or beside affected elements are recorded for the relevant coordination.

  • Paint, finishes and fixed joinery

    Set substrate preparation, retained finishes and the patch boundary against the agreed appearance.

  • Strip-out and reinstatement

    We map removal, making good around former fixtures, material movement and waste. Items outside the brief remain visible as separate decisions rather than being silently assumed.

02 / Joinery and existing finishes at an opening

Use the records to resolve the brief

  • Plans and condition evidence

    Available drawings, photos and the landlord’s item list help identify ambiguities. We compare the brief with the accessible site condition before confirming quantities and scope.

  • Materials and finish decisions

    Confirm material, colour and sheen before ordering. Set work order and finish boundaries around supply and retained surfaces.

Offices & mixed-use buildings ↗

A sequence from protection to handover

Photograph retained finishes before removal work and mark where joinery, partitioning or services meet surfaces that stay. That record gives the team a shared basis for checking repairs at handover.

  1. 01

    Prepare and protect

    We agree access, retained items, work zones and necessary service coordination before removals begin. Deliveries and waste routes are included in preparation.

  2. 02

    Remove, repair and reinstate

    We carry out the agreed strip-out, substrate repairs and coordinated work, recording discoveries that change the original scope before further work proceeds.

  3. 03

    Finish, clear and review

    We complete the agreed finishes and clean-up, then check the item list with your nominated representative and record remaining actions.

Plan around the spaces still in use

An occupied office or shop needs a different sequence from an empty tenancy. We agree staff and customer routes, noise and dust-producing stages, access restrictions and areas being handed back between stages. Drying, curing and related trade attendance are considered when planning those boundaries.

Price the agreed list and close it out

  • Quotation factors

    Quantities, preparation, retained conditions, material matching, access, phasing and waste affect the allowance. Investigation and additional findings are distinguished from agreed reinstatement.

  • Completion against the brief

    We record completed items, agreed appearance and function checks, photographs where included and outstanding work. The handover describes the construction delivered against the approved list.

Check the work against the handback list.

We record what is complete by room or tenancy area, along with approved changes and any unfinished item awaiting review.

  • Agreed handback scope
  • Materials and finish match
  • Close-out by room or tenancy

Common questions

Can you quote from the landlord’s make-good list?
Yes. We compare the list with available records and site conditions, clarify unclear items and prepare an itemised scope for the work to be agreed.
Does a patched wall need repainting beyond the patch?
We review the existing finish, patch position and agreed appearance. Preparation, matching and the boundary of repainting are confirmed in the scope rather than assumed to stop at the damaged area.
What happens if removal reveals additional damage?
We record the finding and explain its effect on the work. Additional repairs, materials or changes are confirmed before being added to the agreed scope.
